speaker: SPEAKER_01
transcript: Well, I suppose you're talking about the bill to dealt with federal employee pay. And there were two parts of that bill. First of all, the bill was not, I felt accurately reported by the media in their initial reports. But first of all, we have some federal employees who are essential employees who are not getting paid. They will get paid when the shutdown ends, but let's say for the sake of argument, the shutdown goes for three months. They will not get paid until that three months is up. I think that's outlandish. I think it was appalling that Republican and Democrat leadership apparently agreed on some sort of compromise in which employees who are working now, such as prison guards, such as the Coast Guard, will not get paid until it's over. I'm opposed to that part of the bill. I was one of only 12 Republicans to co-sponsor bill requiring me to be paid on a timely basis. The other half of the bill dealt with nonessential employees who are not working. A lot of my friends think they should just go on unemployment. I'm willing to give them something, have 60, 70, 80% of their pay. But it seems to me to pay if somebody is not working 100% of their pay when they may not work for four months is a little bit much. It creates a situation in which your employees who are not working are actually in a superior position to the employees who are working. And I've talked to a lot of people over the weekend. They generally agree with me and they have anecdotes in their past where they were laid off or something happened. And they got unemployment insurance and nothing more. And they wondered why the federal employees would get 100% of their pay. I certainly understand we have a moral obligation to give them something. My sympathy goes out to them, but I think a little less than something under 100% of the pay was more appropriate for them. So both halves of the bills I disagree with. I disagree strongly that if you are working, you should have to wait two or three months to get paid and that's horrible. And I really disagree with the idea that when they eventually do get paid, people may not work for three or four months, get 100% of their pay. Usually you have job related expenses, Commuting expenses, maybe parking, maybe daycare. So you're creating a situation which people are better off not working than working, which I don't like.
